title: Barbara Kruger: Money Talks

description.main: Skarstedt Fine Art's 2005 book gathering Barbara Kruger's work on money, with a text by Lisa Phillips.
description.extended:
Money Talks, published by Skarstedt Fine Art in New York in 2005, was the first publication to gather Barbara Kruger's work around a single theme.

The theme is money, a subject Kruger has returned to throughout her career. Lisa Phillips, then director of the New Museum in New York, wrote the text. The book is a 76-page cloth hardcover in a dust jacket.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American artist who pairs found photographs with declarative text. She worked as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, including Mademoiselle, before turning to photocollage in the late 1970s. She received the Golden Lion for lifetime achievement at the 51st Venice Biennale in 2005.

notes: Skarstedt Fine Art, New York, 2005. Hardcover, cloth with dust jacket, 76 pages per most listings (Open Library and the BALTIC library give 80). 11.2 x 8.7 in per Open Library. Text by Lisa Phillips. A bookseller summary describes an original essay by Phillips and two essays by Kruger, and work from the 1980s; this was not confirmed from a publisher or library source, so the description leaves it out. No exhibition tie was confirmed.
